Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-medium-0113", "row_sha256": "401b905b4c1d04d41bcfd5e59fca46f0a681c83876f8f7082b57dbd33670472b", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you draft a short customer support reply for someone whose Alder countertop dishwasher started stopping halfway through a cycle? the customer says it was bought on may 14, 2024, and has sent a photo of the receipt, but we still need to check the purchase date before deciding which route to take. the limited warranty lasts two years from purchase and covers the motor and control board, not cosmetic damage. explain what happens next without saying we know which part failed or promising that the repair is covered. if the purchase date is within the two-year warranty period, ask them to send the receipt and open a service request for review. if it is outside that period, don't submit the issue as warranty-covered; explain that a paid inspection is available instead. keep the two routes separate so the customer can tell what depends on the date check. mention that the warranty doesn't cover cosmetic damage, but don't make it sound like the reported cycle problem is cosmetic. keep the reply straightforward and helpful, and don't add fees, turnaround times, or other warranty terms we haven't been given.", "output": "Write a short, straightforward customer support reply to the owner of an Alder countertop dishwasher that stops halfway through a cycle. The customer reports a purchase date of May 14, 2024, and has sent a photo of the receipt, but the purchase date still needs to be checked before choosing a next step.

The limited warranty lasts two years from purchase and covers the motor and control board, but not cosmetic damage. Do not claim to know which part failed or promise that the repair is covered. Keep these two routes distinct:
- If the purchase date is within the two-year warranty period, ask the customer to send the receipt and open a service request for review.
- If the purchase date is outside that period, do not submit the issue as warranty-covered; explain that a paid inspection is available instead.

Mention that cosmetic damage is not covered without suggesting that the reported cycle problem is cosmetic. Do not add fees, turnaround times, or other warranty terms that have not been provided."}]
